name: Head of IT Operations @ RBC Capital Markets

job_spec.role_overview:
RBC Capital Markets is seeking a Global Head of CM Operations, Regulatory, and Supervisory Technology — a senior technology executive responsible for the full application development lifecycle covering post-execution trade processing (back office), regulatory reporting, and supervisory technology across the Capital Markets division. This is not an infrastructure or production-estate management role; the mandate centres squarely on application ownership, end-to-end product delivery, and the technology strategy underpinning how RBC Capital Markets meets its operational and regulatory obligations at scale. The position reports directly to the Capital Markets Line of Business CIO and carries a standing seat on the CM Tech Operating Committee, placing the incumbent at the heart of divisional technology governance.

The role carries material organisational accountability: a team of approximately 400 technology professionals and an annual budget in the region of $100MM. The incumbent will be the primary technology interface for the CM COO and her management team, translating business priorities into executable technology programmes across the post-trade and regulatory reporting estate. Daily BAU ownership runs in parallel with a live, consequential transformation mandate to simplify and modernise a complex application landscape — improving scale, resilience, and cost efficiency across the division's core operational systems.

The CIO, Vlad Breygin, has set a non-negotiable condition: deep, first-hand knowledge of capital markets is required. Candidates who bring strong technology leadership credentials but lack genuine domain fluency in post-execution trade processing, regulatory reporting frameworks, or the capital markets business model will not meet the bar for this role. The successful candidate will be a technologist who can speak the language of the front and middle office, engage credibly with business and risk stakeholders, and make sound architectural and investment decisions grounded in how capital markets actually operate.
success_metrics: Within 12 months, a credible multi-year simplification and modernisation roadmap for the CM Operations and Regulatory Technology estate is agreed with the CIO and CM COO, with legacy application decommission targets, platform consolidation milestones, and investment phasing signed off through the CM Tech Operating Committee.

By month 18, measurable improvement in system resilience and operational stability across post-trade processing platforms — defined by agreed SLAs, reduction in major incident frequency, and audit-ready evidence of improved scale capacity — is demonstrable to the COO's management team.

Regulatory and supervisory reporting technology obligations are delivered on time and in full across all applicable jurisdictions throughout the first year, with zero material regulatory reporting failures attributable to technology gaps and a structured forward plan for emerging reporting mandates.

The approximately 400-person technology organisation is operating with clear leadership accountability at each layer, talent retention across senior engineering roles meets or exceeds divisional benchmarks, and the function is assessed by the CIO as a high-performing delivery organisation capable of sustaining concurrent run and change responsibilities.
required_experience: Demonstrated ownership of application development for post-execution trade processing — including clearing, settlement, reconciliation, or related back-office workflows — at a global investment bank or equivalent capital markets firm; infrastructure or production-estate IT operations experience does not satisfy this requirement.

Proven leadership of a large-scale technology organisation at head-of or managing-director level, with direct accountability for a team in the range of several hundred technologists (including managers-of-managers) and a budget of $75MM or greater.

Deep, practitioner-level knowledge of capital markets — including the mechanics of post-trade processing across at least one major asset class (equities, fixed income, FX, rates, or credit) and the regulatory reporting obligations that govern them — sufficient to engage as a credible peer with the CM CIO, COO, and front-office stakeholders.

Hands-on experience delivering regulatory or supervisory reporting technology in a regulated capital markets environment, with named exposure to at least one applicable framework (e.g. MiFID II, EMIR, Dodd-Frank, Reg SCI, CAT, or Basel III/IV) and direct accountability for technology responses to regulatory change programmes.

Evidenced leadership of a major technology transformation programme within a capital markets context — including platform modernisation, legacy simplification, or application estate consolidation — with a named programme, defined budget, and quantifiable outcome; generic change-leadership experience without these artefacts does not meet the bar.

Track record of operating as a senior technology executive interfacing directly with business COO or CFO-level stakeholders, translating regulatory and operational requirements into funded technology programmes and governing delivery through formal operating committee structures.
key_responsibilities: Own the global application development portfolio spanning post-execution trade processing, regulatory reporting, and supervisory technology, holding full accountability for roadmap, investment prioritisation, and delivery outcomes across approximately 400 engineers and technologists.

Lead the simplification and modernisation transformation of the CM Operations and Regulatory technology estate, establishing measurable milestones for legacy decommission, platform consolidation, and improved system resilience at scale.

Manage a technology budget of approximately $100MM per annum, governing capex and opex allocation across run-the-bank and change-the-bank programmes with rigour and transparency to the CM Tech Operating Committee.

Interface directly with the CM COO and her management team as the accountable technology partner for back-office trade processing and regulatory reporting, translating operational and compliance requirements into funded, time-bound technology initiatives.

Drive delivery of regulatory and supervisory reporting technology obligations, ensuring platforms remain current with evolving regulatory frameworks and that the division can respond rapidly to new reporting mandates from applicable regulators.

Establish and maintain engineering discipline, delivery governance, and quality standards across the application development function, building a performance culture that can sustain both BAU reliability and concurrent transformation at scale.

Build and retain senior technology leadership within the function, developing managers-of-managers across the global team and ensuring succession depth across critical domains including post-trade systems, data engineering, and regulatory technology.
Represent CM Operations and Regulatory Technology on the CM Tech Operating Committee, providing clear, business-grounded input to divisional technology strategy and operating model decisions.
leadership_culture_fit: Genuine capital markets domain fluency — the candidate must hold substantive knowledge of how the post-trade and regulatory reporting landscape operates, not merely familiarity acquired through adjacency; the CIO has stated this as a first-principles requirement and it will be tested in the interview process.

Operator mindset at scale — comfortable holding simultaneous accountability for BAU reliability and a live transformation mandate without allowing either to degrade; demonstrates clear prioritisation frameworks and the credibility to make trade-off decisions in front of senior business and technology stakeholders.

Trusted business partner to non-technology executives — able to engage the CM COO and her management team in the language of risk, regulatory obligation, and business outcome rather than technology abstraction, and to translate complex engineering constraints into decisions that business leadership can act on.

Talent builder with managers-of-managers experience — has demonstrably grown and retained senior engineering leadership within large organisations, understands the difference between managing a team and building an organisation, and can sustain performance culture through periods of significant structural change.

calibration.inferred_scope: This is a senior leadership role overseeing IT operations for RBC Capital Markets, the investment banking and capital markets division of Royal Bank of Canada. The role likely carries global or regional (North America/EMEA) scope and reports into a CTO or CIO function within the division.
calibration.weights_rationale: The recruiter's priority signals all scored 9–10, with Capital Markets domain expertise explicitly flagged by the CIO stakeholder as non-negotiable and domain/technical/leadership each weighted at maximum, driving those three dimensions to the top of the model; the must-haves around regulatory and supervisory technology ownership, a $100MM budget, 400-person team, and a live modernisation/simplification mandate further elevate regulatory and transformation dimensions above baseline for a global investment bank context.

culture_profile.summary: RBC Capital Markets presents as a regulated, matrix-structured global investment bank where capital-markets domain depth and operational scale are non-negotiable. Feedback signals are placeholder/test entries only, so cultural calibration rests entirely on the role brief and industry context.

red_flags.label: IT Operations vs App Dev confusion — anti-pattern risk
red_flags.detail: The hiring manager explicitly flags that candidates confusing Ops IT (infrastructure run) with application development will fail screening. Recruiters must verify the candidate owns software delivery and post-trade application roadmaps, not just production estate management.

red_flags.label: Domain depth gap — capital markets specificity required
red_flags.detail: CIO Vlad Breygin's sole stated filter is deep capital-markets knowledge. Candidates from adjacent fintech, wealth management, or generic banking technology without named asset-class or post-trade system ownership (e.g. Murex, Broadridge, FIS GMI) will likely be screened out regardless of leadership scale.

red_flags.label: Scale mismatch — sub-threshold leadership scope
red_flags.detail: Role requires managers-of-managers experience across ~400 headcount and $100MM budget. Candidates who cannot cite direct headcount, total org span, and owned budget explicitly cannot credibly compete; any CV silent on these numbers must have the gap flagged before submission.

red_flags.label: Feedback signal vacuum — cultural calibration limited
red_flags.detail: All three HM feedback entries are test/placeholder content with no substantive preference signal. Culture profile confidence is constrained to industry and role-brief inference; recalibration is warranted once real interview feedback is captured.

risk_appetite.evidence: Global investment bank operating under FCA/PRA, OSC/OSFI, and SEC/FINRA regulatory regimes; the mandate to modernise post-trade and regulatory reporting technology signals appetite for controlled change within a compliance-bounded envelope — not speculative innovation.

decision_speed.evidence: The role reports to a Line of Business CIO and sits on the CM Tech Operating Committee, with direct CM COO interface; multi-stakeholder governance and a $100MM budget imply board/committee approval cycles rather than founder-speed execution.

change_readiness.evidence: The estate modernisation is described as simplifying and modernising for scale and resilience — a structured, risk-managed programme rather than a blank-sheet transformation. A regulated capital-markets environment with large incumbent post-trade infrastructure (likely Murex/Calypso-class systems) points to incremental rather than wholesale change readiness.

leadership_preference.evidence: Must-haves explicitly call out BAU ownership of a 400-person team, $100MM budget management, and a transformation mandate grounded in simplification and resilience — delivery execution over strategic narrative. CIO stakeholder focus on capital-markets domain depth reinforces operator over visionary profile.

culture_profile.candidate_facing_pitch: RBC Capital Markets is a globally regulated investment bank where this role sits at the intersection of post-trade technology and regulatory reporting at serious scale — 400 people, $100MM budget, direct COO and CIO visibility. The trade-off is honest: this is a disciplined, committee-governed environment that rewards deep capital-markets domain expertise and operational delivery over frontier experimentation.

intelligence_report.ai_agenda:
RBC Capital Markets has one of the most concrete and publicly documented AI agendas among global investment banks. The Aiden platform ecosystem — built with RBC Borealis on Nvidia AI Enterprise — is the flagship, encompassing electronic trading (VWAP and Arrival Price deep reinforcement learning algorithms), research acceleration (AidenResearch, QuickTakes built on Databricks), and banker productivity (AidenBanker). As of a March 2026 PYMNTS report, more than 8,000 capital markets employees are already using the Aiden platform. RBC Borealis has filed more than 635 AI-related patents since 2019 and the ATOM foundation model was used across 15 products and processes in 2025. RBC partnered with Cohere in 2025 to develop secure generative AI solutions for financial services, and with Nvidia for customised generative AI deployment. RBC's 2025 Investor Day set a target of $700M–$1B in pre-tax earnings from AI-driven initiatives by 2027, and the firm ranks first in Canada and third globally in the 2025 Evident AI Index.

For the specific mandate of this role, the AI agenda is most directly relevant through its implications for supervisory and regulatory reporting automation and the potential to embed AI-driven controls and exception management into back-office workflows. While public documentation on AI deployment within the post-trade and regulatory estate is limited (the public narrative is front-office and research focused), the firm's broader AI Group — reporting directly to CEO Dave McKay — has a mandate to scale AI across all business segments, including operations. A candidate who can credibly connect the firm's AI infrastructure (Aiden platform, Databricks, Lumina) to back-office modernisation use cases will resonate strongly with Vlad Breygin and the CM Tech Operating Committee.
red_flags: Candidates whose back-office or operations technology experience is as a consumer of systems (e.g. business analyst, product owner sitting above a vendor platform) rather than as an application development owner with roadmap and vendor-contract accountability will not clear Vlad Breygin's domain depth bar.

Pure infrastructure or IT Operations (run-the-bank, SRE, ITSM) backgrounds are an explicit anti-pattern called out in the recruiter brief — the role is application development leadership for post-trade processing, not production estate management.

Candidates without managers-of-managers experience at a comparable headcount (~300–500 resources) and budget (~$75M–$125M) cannot be presented for a Head-of role of this scope; the leadership dimension gap must be stated explicitly if headcount or budget numbers are absent from the CV.

Executives who have spent the majority of their careers in pure consulting or advisory without operational P&L and team ownership tend to lack the daily BAU accountability culture that a COO-interfacing technology leadership role demands at a firm of RBC's regulatory weight.

Candidates who can speak to AI and digital innovation at the front-office level but have no post-trade or regulatory reporting depth will be filtered quickly by the CIO given the explicit Capital Markets domain non-negotiable — surface-level capital markets familiarity is insufficient.

Strong general banking technology leaders from retail, wealth, or commercial banking divisions who have not operated within a broker-dealer or investment bank post-trade environment will face a steep credibility gap on the specific regulatory reporting and clearing/settlement infrastructure required by this role.

intelligence_report.executive_summary:
RBC Capital Markets is operating from a position of deliberate technology investment and transformation, with the Capital Markets division explicitly identified as a growth engine within Royal Bank of Canada's broader enterprise strategy. The firm operates 55 offices across 16 countries and, as of February 2026, employs approximately 11,000 people with estimated annual revenues of $15 billion. The CM Tech function is structured around a Line of Business CIO model — the hiring stakeholder is Vlad Breygin, Capital Markets CIO — with a standing CM Tech Operating Committee that the incoming Global Head of CM Operations, Regulatory, and Supervisory Technology will join. The mandate is unambiguous: the role owns all application development for post-execution trade processing (back office) and regulatory/supervisory reporting technology, carries a ~$100MM annual budget and ~400 headcount, and is chartered to drive a major simplification and modernisation initiative across the estate for scale and resilience.

The firm's public posture is biased toward in-house build: the Aiden algorithmic trading platform (built with RBC Borealis using deep reinforcement learning), the Lumina enterprise data and AI platform, the ATOM proprietary foundation model, and the AidenResearch/AidenBanker product suite are all internally developed. In May 2025, RBC Capital Markets formalised a dedicated AI and Digital Innovation team under Lindsay Patrick (Chief Strategy and Innovation Officer) and Bobby Grubert (Head of AI and Digital Innovation). RBC's 2025 Investor Day cited $700M–$1B in pre-tax earnings targeted by 2027 from AI-driven initiatives, and the firm ranked first in Canada and third globally in the 2025 Evident AI Index. The technology posture for back-office and regulatory technology, while less publicly profiled than the front-office AI story, sits squarely in the mandate of this hire — the incumbent will need to translate the firm's front-office innovation ambition into the resilience and simplification of the post-trade and regulatory reporting estate, interfacing daily with the CM COO and her management team.
intelligence_report.technology_strategy:
RBC Capital Markets operates a strongly in-house build posture for strategic technology. Confirmed proprietary platforms include Aiden (deep reinforcement learning electronic trading, launched globally 2020), Lumina (enterprise data and AI platform), ATOM (foundation model for financial services built by RBC Borealis with 100+ researchers, deployed across 15 products and processes in 2025), AidenResearch (AI agents for earnings content, call summarisation, and filing access), AidenBanker (pitchbook and meeting-prep automation), and QuickTakes (research turnaround platform built on Databricks). The disclosed tech stack includes Microsoft, Java, C#, Power BI, and SQL Server. For the post-trade and regulatory estate, the firm's stated goal — sourced from the recruiter brief — is simplification and modernisation for scale and resilience, signalling that the current estate carries legacy complexity typical of a mid-tier global investment bank that has grown through product and geographic expansion. Project Samara (Canada's first blockchain-based bond issuance, settled via distributed ledger in partnership with the Bank of Canada and RBC Investor Services) signals an appetite for post-trade infrastructure experimentation. RBC Clear, a purpose-built digital-first cash management platform launched in 2024–25, won the 2025 Model Bank award for Reinventing Cash Management, reflecting the firm's willingness to decommission legacy workflows and build from scratch when the business case is clear.

The CM technology organisation is governed through a Line of Business CIO model with a standing CM Tech Operating Committee, which the incoming head will join as a standing member. This governance structure implies a reasonably mature technology operating model with cross-functional accountability — budget holders sit alongside the business COO and CIO, not below them. The $100MM annual technology budget for the Operations, Regulatory, and Supervisory Technology tower is material and indicates the firm is prepared to fund the modernisation programme at scale, not incrementally.
intelligence_report.ideal_candidate_profile:
The target archetype is a senior technology executive who has owned — not just contributed to — the post-execution application development estate at a global investment bank or large broker-dealer, with credible capital markets domain depth across equities, fixed income, or multi-asset post-trade. The role carries a $100MM annual budget and ~400 headcount, so the candidate must have demonstrated managers-of-managers leadership at comparable scale; direct headcount and budget ownership must be named and verifiable, not inferred. The standing membership on the CM Tech Operating Committee and the daily interface with the CM COO require executive maturity: the ability to translate complex technology states into business risk language for non-technical COO-level stakeholders, and to hold ground on architectural decisions under commercial pressure. Given the firm's confirmed in-house build posture and proprietary platform investments, candidates from pure third-party system integrator or outsourced operations backgrounds will likely struggle to earn credibility with the engineering-heavy RBC Borealis-influenced technology culture.

On transformation, the mandate explicitly requires driving a simplification and modernisation initiative — the Post-Trade Systems Check skill applies in full here. Candidates must be able to name at least one analogous programme with budget, duration, platforms decommissioned or migrated, and measurable outcome (e.g. settlement fail-rate improvement, regulatory submission latency reduction, system consolidation from N to M). Regulatory exposure is non-negotiable: the role owns supervisory and regulatory reporting technology, so familiarity with SEC Rule 15c3-3, CAT, Reg SCI, and/or EMIR/MiFID II reporting infrastructure (depending on geography) must be demonstrable by named programme, not generic compliance language. Candidates who have navigated a T+1 readiness programme, a regulatory remediation driven by SEC/FINRA/FCA findings, or a CCP/clearing-house integration bring concrete differentiation that maps directly to the stated scope.
